findings.observation: The compositor renders a bounded batch of at most 32 pending damage tiles per loop. Retained surfaces are supported through the window-session receiver.
Validated opaque body tiles use a direct backing-buffer copy; tiles intersecting chrome, pointer, dock or palette use the composite renderer.

Tiles remain serialized through bounded SUR1 messages and per-tile acknowledgement. The existing performance contract documents 22,386 requests and 3,198 replies for a 1,248x656 app surface at 1280x720. Changing this requires a versioned protocol and native gates.

decision: No native code change: the inspected paths already have damage batching, retained-frame support and an oracle-tested raster fast path. Further changes to per-tile IPC would affect a shared interface and are not justified without the unavailable native test/toolchain and workload measurements.
evidence_boundary: Source inspection only. No native test, QEMU run, browser benchmark, latency, CPU, memory or energy measurement was performed.
